title: Tinubu Orders 500 More CNG Stations, Targets Lower Transport Fares Nationwide
excerpt: President Bola Tinubu has ordered the deployment of 500 additional Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) refuelling stations, bringing the federal government's target to 1,000 stations nationwide — part of continuing efforts to cut transport costs for everyday Nigerians, including millions of Yoruba families in the Southwest.
content:
As part of the ongoing Presidential CNG Initiative (PCNGI), President Tinubu has directed the rollout of 500 more CNG stations nationwide, doubling the original target to 1,000. The expansion is aimed at giving commercial and private transporters — including in Lagos, Oyo, Ogun, Osun, Ondo, and Ekiti — a cheaper, cleaner alternative to petrol, helping to bring down the cost of transportation for ordinary citizens.

This builds on the administration's broader energy reform agenda following the removal of the petrol subsidy, with the CNG program designed to cushion the transition and improve affordability across Yoruba-populated states and beyond.

title: The House That Became a Shrine: Inside Susanne Wenger's Sacred Osogbo Home
excerpt: A look inside the preserved Osogbo home of the late Austrian-born artist and Yoruba priestess Susanne Wenger, whose life work helped save the Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove and popularize Yoruba art worldwide.
content:
Susanne Wenger, who became a devotee of Ọ̀ṣun and a driving force behind the preservation of the Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove (now a UNESCO World Heritage Site), left behind a home in Osogbo that has become a place of pilgrimage and cultural significance.

Read the full feature at the source link for more on her legacy and the New Sacred Art movement she helped inspire.

title: Welcome to Ìròyìn — Our New Yoruba Community News Page
excerpt: We're launching Ìròyìn, a curated news space dedicated to stories from and about the Yoruba community worldwide — culture, royalty, diaspora life, and more.
content:
Welcome to **Ìròyìn** — meaning "news" or "report" in Yoruba. This page will feature carefully selected news relevant to Yoruba people and culture worldwide, curated by our editorial team rather than automated feeds, to ensure everything here is genuinely meaningful to our community.

Check back regularly for updates on royal palace news, diaspora community events, language preservation efforts, and more.

title: \"Why I Prostrate to Oba Even as a Muslim\": Femi Adebayo Opens Up on Yoruba Culture
excerpt: Nollywood actor and filmmaker Femi Adebayo discusses how Yoruba tradition and religious identity coexist in his life, reflecting on respect for traditional rulers regardless of personal faith.
content:
In a candid interview, popular Yoruba actor and producer Femi Adebayo — known for films like "Jagun Jagun" and "King of Thieves" — spoke about the enduring importance of prostrating before an Oba (traditional ruler) as an act of cultural respect, regardless of one's religious background.

title: Ebumawe of Ago-Iwoye Seeks Stronger Youth Engagement to Preserve Heritage
excerpt: The Ebumawe of Ago-Iwoye, Oba Rasak Adenugba, has called for stronger youth engagement and institutional support to preserve the town's Yoruba cultural heritage for future generations.
content:
The traditional ruler of Ago-Iwoye in Ogun State, Oba Rasak Adenugba (the Ebumawe), has highlighted the urgent need for greater youth involvement and institutional backing to safeguard the town's rich Yoruba cultural heritage.

title: Tinubu Urges Banks to Turn Recapitalisation Into Jobs and Production
excerpt: President Tinubu has challenged Nigeria's banking and financial sector to move beyond traditional financial intermediation, urging that the ongoing bank recapitalisation exercise translate directly into job creation and increased local production.
content:
Speaking on the outcomes of Nigeria's bank recapitalisation drive, President Bola Tinubu called on financial institutions to channel the freshly raised capital into productive investment — manufacturing, agriculture, and job-creating enterprises — rather than short-term financial plays.

The recapitalisation program, part of the administration's broader economic reform agenda, is intended to strengthen the banking sector's capacity to fund large-scale industrial and infrastructure projects across the country, including in the Southwest's manufacturing and agribusiness hubs.
